# Personal Agent Naming: agentnaming.ai

> Personal Agent Naming is an open standard for naming personal agents.
> A handle is a name you choose on the email you
> already have (`<name>.<email>`, for example `PublicAgent.ann@gmail.com`),
> bound to your agent's key, and resolvable to a signed card listing the
> addresses where the agent can be reached. It names agents and works with any
> transport. This site explains the standard; nothing is claimed or paired here.

## Getting a name

- Any registrar that follows the specification can give an agent a name:
  https://agentnaming.ai/get-a-name.html
- One registrar that follows the specification: https://naming.agentmesh.ai
- The open-source registrar, to run your own: https://github.com/AgentNaming/pan-registrar
- The specification: https://agentnaming.ai/spec.html

## Resolution (public, no account)

Any conforming registrar serves these paths and works the same way. The
examples use the registrar at https://naming.agentmesh.ai.

- `GET https://naming.agentmesh.ai/api/resolve?handle=<full-handle>`
- WebFinger: `GET https://naming.agentmesh.ai/.well-known/webfinger?resource=acct:<handle>`
- The registrar's signing keys: `GET https://naming.agentmesh.ai/api/registrar-key`

## Example handle

`example.agent@commonagent.net` is a handle whose domain serves its own records,
which outrank any registrar's. It exists only as an example: its key was made for
it, and no agent runs behind it.

- WebFinger: `GET https://commonagent.net/.well-known/webfinger?resource=acct:example.agent@commonagent.net`
- The card the record links to: `GET https://commonagent.net/api/card/example.agent.json`
- The domain's signing keys: `GET https://commonagent.net/api/registrar-key`

## Reference

- [What it is](https://agentnaming.ai/)
- [For implementers](https://agentnaming.ai/implementers.html)
- [Agent Messaging](https://agentmessaging.ai/), the messaging standard it is a companion to
